protections: Every request body the daemon will parse and act on must be shown to the authorization plugins, or the request refused: HTTP framing (declared Content-Length, chunked/undeclared length, oversized, non-JSON media type) must not let a plugin decide on an empty body while the daemon acts on the real body.
The authorization plugin must see the response status/headers/body before any of it reaches the client, so it can deny or filter privileged content.
Registry credentials must not reach authorization plugins: Authorization / X-Registry-Auth headers are stripped and the /auth request body is skipped.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The capture has a documented 1MB cap (maxBodySize) and the existing TestDrainBody explicitly asserts that a 2MB body yields a zero-length capture, so a solver can read the skip as intended behaviour; the plugin still receives the Content-Length header and could refuse the request itself.

The earlier 0-length fix already routes chunked requests into drainBody through isChunked, so the chunked framing looks covered; drainBody's full-buffer branch returns (nil, newBody, nil) with only a warning, which reads like a normal 'too large to copy' outcome rather than a bypass.

sendBody documents that 'body is sent only for text or json messages', and most JSON endpoints call CheckForJSON, so it is easy to assume a request with a non-JSON or absent Content-Type is a client error the plugin need not see; in fact these handlers decode JSON from the body regardless of the declared media type, so the plugin is handed an empty body for a spec the daemon executes.

The 64KB maxBufferSize is an explicit memory bound (with a TODO), and the plugin still receives the status code and headers; every streaming endpoint (/events, /logs, /build, /pull, hijacked exec) has to flush as it goes, so 'the plugin only sees the tail of a large response' looks like an accepted limitation rather than a bypass.

The authz plugin is a trusted policy component and the /auth body only feeds registry authentication, never an authorization decision; the skip is three lines in sendBody and looks like a harmless optimisation, so there is no obvious security impact to chase.

masking: T1's Content-Length precondition keeps drainBody (T2) from ever seeing a declared-length request, so the overflow branch at authz.go:149-154 is reachable only through chunked/undeclared lengths; a fixer who edits only the caller never exercises the helper.

Once T1 is closed by rejecting on Content-Length, a chunked/undeclared-length request is the remaining oversized route, and a test suite that only sets a large Content-Length reports the bug as fixed.

T3 is masked by the assumption that every JSON endpoint calls CheckForJSON; the five handlers that do not (swarm, plugin, checkpoint, system/auth, image push) are the ones nobody re-reads after changing sendBody.

conflicts.what: Making the plugin see every body the daemon parses (T3's natural fix) means unbounded bodies for build/cp/load/import tar streams; the maxBodySize cap that T1/T2's fix must keep, and that the 10MB CopyToContainer and image load tests exercise, forbids buffering them, so the T3 rule has to be media-type and streaming aware rather than 'always send the body'.

Loosening or removing the media-type gate in sendBody to close T3 sends the /auth body (registry credentials) to plugins, which the auth-endpoint rule at authz.go:180 and the integration helper's assertBody invariant say must be withheld; the T3 fix must keep an auth-endpoint skip that actually matches real request paths while not withholding other bodies.

fairness_risks: Archive/streaming uploads must keep working: TestAuthzPluginEnsureContainerCopyToFrom sends a ~10MB tar (integration/plugin/authz/authz_plugin_test.go:401-435) and image load/import stream tars (:348-385); a rule that requires the plugin to see the body must not buffer, truncate or refuse these.

Streaming responses must keep working: the event-stream test (:213-275) plus /build, /pull, /logs and hijacked exec write incrementally; a T4 fix that withholds a response until AuthZResponse returns would break them.

Large legitimate JSON request bodies (container/service create with large Env, Mounts or Config payloads) would be refused by a blanket 'reject a body you cannot fully inspect' rule; the daemon publishes no smaller-body contract (pkg/authorization/authz.go:18 is the only limit).

Registry auth must stay hidden from plugins: headers() strips Authorization and X-Registry-Auth (pkg/authorization/authz.go:196-207) and the integration plugin asserts it (integration/plugin/authz/main_test.go:157-165), so 'show the plugin everything' cannot be the T3 fix.

The existing unit test TestDrainBody asserts the vulnerable behaviour (pkg/authorization/authz_unix_test.go:142-173, especially :149), so the task must allow the solver to change that test; keeping it green keeps the bypass.
POST /auth must keep accepting credential bodies (api/server/router/system/system_routes.go:217-232) after any T6 fix; only the copy sent to the plugin may be withheld.

design.why: Five traps, five edits, four layers. T1 is the bug the report names (declared Content-Length >= 1MB is skipped) and is mainly calibration; T2 is the same guard reached through a chunked/undeclared length, where drainBody returns (nil, newBody, nil) with only a warning. T1 and T2 are listed as separate groups because a single-site fix at authz.go:73 (reject on Content-Length) leaves T2, and a drainBody-only edit leaves T1, so neither site alone closes the pair - though one policy ('refuse a body you cannot fully inspect') closes both, and if a grader collapses them the design is still four independent traps. T3 is the deepseek trap: a route where the plugin's body visibility never existed - five router files (swarm init/join/update/services/secrets/configs, plugin pull/upgrade/set, checkpoint create, system /auth, image push) decode JSON without enforcing the media type that sendBody keys on - with an easy dismissal ('plugins only get JSON bodies'). T4 is the mimo trap: a how-type ordering bug where responseModifier flushes 64KB chunks to the client before AuthZResponse, so the plugin sees only the tail; the naive fix (buffer the whole response) breaks /events, /logs, /build, /pull and hijacked exec, which the existing integration tests require. T6 is the dead path validation the earlier fix left behind: isAuthEndpoint's regexp expects a host-prefixed URL but is given url.Parse(...).Path, which always starts with '/', so the /auth body (registry credentials) always reaches the plugin, contradicting authz.go:180 and the integration helper's assertBody invariant. Dismissal reasons are all different: 'the 1MB cap is intentional and tested' (T1/T2), 'only JSON bodies are promised' (T3), 'the 64KB buffer is a deliberate memory bound' (T4), 'the plugin is trusted' (T6). The design beats a single-bug task because each trap needs a different edit in a different layer (body-capture precondition, drain helper, router body parsing, response writer, path regexp) and a fix for one never closes another; it beats adding more router routes because T3 already covers them as one media-type group, and it beats a T1+T2-only design because that one has no deepseek-type far route and no mimo-type coupled/streaming constraint.

unverified: The pre-A form of the AuthZRequest condition and the content of b_fix e89edb19ad7d are not present in this checkout; whether the `r.ContentLength < maxBodySize` clause was written by A (regression) or predates it (incomplete fix) cannot be verified here. The candidate record classifies the link as 'incomplete fix', which is what b_in_code_a_wrote=false reflects.

The claim that r.RequestURI is origin-form (leading '/') for real daemon requests is net/http server behaviour outside the repository. Even for absolute-form targets, url.Parse(...).Path keeps the leading '/', so isAuthEndpoint would still not match.

The claim that Go's net/http server deletes the Transfer-Encoding header before the middleware runs (so a plugin sees neither Content-Length nor Transfer-Encoding on a chunked request) is stdlib behaviour, not visible in this tree.

Whether the daemon's TLS listener ever negotiates HTTP/2 is not verifiable here; a body with ContentLength == -1 and no chunked encoding would also skip the capture at authz.go:73. api/server/server.go:58-62 builds the http.Server without a TLSConfig, which suggests h2 is not enabled.

No test in the tree exercises a >64KB JSON response through AuthZResponse; the flush-before-authorization claim is derived from response.go:125-127, :169-178 and :181-204 and the call order at middleware.go:85 and :99.
The upstream intent for oversized bodies (reject versus buffer/stream to the plugin) is unknown; both change the expectations codified in TestDrainBody (authz_unix_test.go:149).

The volume of legitimate >1MB JSON creates is not evidenced by any test in the tree; the fairness risk is inferred from the API surface (container create config, service spec) rather than demonstrated.
